newsitem.title: USA: Thermo Ecotek says fire losses minimal.
newsitem.headline: Thermo Ecotek says fire losses minimal.

text.p: Thermo Ecotek Corp said Thursday that it expects losses related to a fire at its Wyoming clean-coal plant to amount to less than three percent of its total plant investment.
The fire destroyed one of two oil heaters and an auxiliary oil storage tank at the plant, which is owned jointly with KFx Inc, but it did not affect four coal processors, the company said.
Thermo Electron said repair costs are expected to be covered by insurance.
The company did not disclose the total plant investment. A spokesman did not immediately return a telephone call seeking further information.
The plant is designed to produce coal known as K-Fuel by transforming low-energy coal into cleaner-burning, high-energy fuel.

Thermo Electron said the fire occurred during a recess from a series of test runs prior to full commercial operation. The company said it expects a new auxiliary oil tank will be installed in the next two months when startup procedures using the remaining oil heater will continue.
Full output at an annualized rate of 500,000 tons per year will be delayed while the second heater and tank are being replaced, it said.
A company spokeswoman said the equipment losses were estimated at between $2 million and $3 million.
